title: Global Stocks Surge, Tech Shares Rebound as U.S. Markets Close for Thanksgiving
body:
Shares across Europe and Asia climbed on Thursday, buoyed by renewed interest in artificial‑intelligence‑related equities, even as Wall Street remained silent for the Thanksgiving holiday. The rally lifted major indices in London, Frankfurt and Tokyo, while the Shanghai Composite and Hong Kong’s Hang Seng also posted modest gains. Traders cited a fresh wave of buying in AI‑focused firms as the primary catalyst, though analysts warned that the sector’s recent volatility could temper enthusiasm in the days ahead.

In Europe, the FTSE 100 rose 0.4 percent, the DAX added 0.5 percent and the CAC 40 edged up 0.3 percent, each bolstered by gains in technology and semiconductor stocks. London‑listed AI specialist Graphcore and German chipmaker Infineon were among the top performers, reflecting investors’ appetite for companies positioned to supply the hardware and software infrastructure behind generative AI models. Meanwhile, the United Kingdom’s financial‑services sector saw a modest pullback, as traders took profits after a week of strong earnings reports.

Across the Pacific, Japan’s Nikkei 225 climbed 0.6 percent, driven largely by a surge in the shares of SoftBank Group and its AI‑focused Vision Fund portfolio companies. In Hong Kong, the Hang Seng index rose 0.2 percent, with notable lifts in Chinese AI startups that have recently listed on the STAR Market. Shanghai’s market followed suit, gaining 0.3 percent as investors poured money into domestic AI chip producers seeking to reduce reliance on U.S. technology. The broader Asian rally was underpinned by a weaker U.S. dollar, which made export‑oriented stocks more attractive to foreign investors.

The AI rally comes after a week of mixed sentiment toward the sector. Earlier in the month, several high‑profile AI stocks experienced sharp sell‑offs amid concerns that valuations had become detached from fundamentals and that regulatory scrutiny could intensify. Yet the latest buying spree suggests that investors are once again betting on the long‑term growth potential of AI, especially as major corporations announce new deployments of large‑language models and generative tools. “We’re seeing a classic ‘buy the rumor, sell the news’ pattern,” said Maria Liu, a senior analyst at GlobalEquities Research. “The hype around AI has cooled slightly, but the underlying demand for compute power and data services remains robust.”

Despite the upbeat tone, market participants remain cautious about the sustainability of the rally. The AI trade has been volatile, with some stocks swinging double‑digit percentages within days. Moreover, the broader macro environment—still marked by sticky inflation, a gradual slowdown in global growth, and geopolitical tensions—could limit risk appetite. Central banks in the Eurozone and Japan are maintaining accommodative policies, but any surprise rate hike or adverse economic data could quickly reverse the gains seen in tech‑heavy indices.

Looking ahead, the next few weeks will be critical for the AI narrative. Upcoming earnings reports from leading chipmakers and cloud providers, as well as policy statements from regulators in the United States, Europe and China, could either reinforce the sector’s momentum or spark a correction. For now, the global market’s upward trajectory, powered by AI‑centric buying, offers a hopeful sign for risk‑on investors, but the underlying volatility reminds traders that the AI boom is still in its early, often turbulent, stages.
